To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
global integrated assessment models are currently not well-equipped to address the challenges of the water-energy-land nexus.

(1) global integrated assessment models have made significant advances in representing the nexus between water, energy and agriculture; (2) the current state of the science is still far from representing all relevant interactions; (3) there is a need for improved data, model development and computational capacity to address these challenges; and (4) there is a pressing need for global integrated assessment modelers to collaborate more closely in developing a shared vision of the future.
global integrated assessment models have not yet fully risen to the challenge of modeling solutions to the water-energy-land nexus.
